q.s: The Harappan site of Dholavira in the Rann of Kutch is known locally by which name?
q.x: Dholavira on Khadir island in Kutch is locally called Kotada; Kot Bala is Balakot in Baluchistan.

q.s: The name of the Harappan site Kalibangan in Rajasthan literally means:
q.x: Kalibangan means 'black bangles', after the bangle fragments found at the site.

q.s: Dholavira, one of the five largest Harappan cities, was built mainly of which material, unlike most Harappan sites?
q.x: Dholavira used dressed sandstone and limestone blocks, whereas most Harappan cities used baked bricks.

q.s: The Harappan dockyard at Lothal was connected with which water body?
q.x: Lothal's dock was joined to the Gulf of Khambhat (Cambay) through a channel.

q.s: Which of the following was the westernmost port of the Harappan civilisation?
q.x: Sutkagendor on the Makran coast of Baluchistan was the westernmost Harappan site and port.

q.s: In the Sindhi language, the name of the Harappan city Mohenjodaro means:
q.x: Mohenjodaro means 'Mound of the Dead' in Sindhi; Lothal means the same in Gujarati.

q.s: The Harappans were the first to grow cotton, which the Greeks called by which name?
q.x: The Greeks called cotton Sindon (from Sind); Meluhha was the Mesopotamian name for the Indus region.

q.s: Which of the following crops was NOT grown by the Harappans?
q.x: Maize is an American crop introduced much later; wheat, barley, sesame and mustard were Harappan crops.

q.s: Evidence of salt production in the Harappan period has been found at which site in Gujarat?
q.x: Kerala-no-dhoro (Padri) has yielded evidence of salt making; Kuntasi had bead and copper workshops.

q.s: Faience, called the world's first glazed ware, was used by the Harappans mainly for making:
q.x: Faience, ground silica glazed blue-green, was used for beads, bangles, amulets and small figurines.

q.s: In the Rigvedic period, the term 'Karmara' referred to which craftsman?
q.x: Karmara was the smith; the potter was Kulala and the goldsmith Hiranyakara.

q.s: In the Rigvedic economy, the craftsman called 'Takshan' was a:
q.x: Takshan was the carpenter (chariot maker); Kulala was the potter and Vaya the weaver.

q.s: Which Rigvedic term denoted the potter?
q.x: Kulala was the potter; Bhishak was the physician and Hiranyakara the goldsmith.

q.s: The rules followed by guilds (shrenis) in ancient India were called:
q.x: Guilds framed their own rules, shreni-dharma, and fixed prices and wages; their head was the jetthaka.

q.s: Rajghat, which has yielded punch-marked coins and seals with Greek inscriptions, is a site near:
q.x: Rajghat lies in Varanasi and is a key site of the Second Urbanisation in the Ganga valley.

q.s: In Buddhism, Right View and Right Intention of the Eightfold Path together form:
q.x: Right View and Right Intention form Prajna (wisdom); speech, action and livelihood form Sila.

q.s: Which of the following elements of the Eightfold Path does NOT belong to Sila (ethical conduct)?
q.x: Right Mindfulness belongs to Samadhi along with Right Effort and Right Concentration.

q.s: The Buddha performed the 'Twin Miracle' at which place?
q.x: The Twin Miracle took place at Shravasti, where the Buddha also gave most of his sermons.

q.s: Which of the following rock-cut caves belong to the Mauryan period?
q.x: The Barabar caves in Bihar date to the Mauryan age (3rd century BCE); Karla is Satavahana period.

q.s: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was built under the patronage of which dynasty?
q.x: The Kailasa temple was carved under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I in the 8th century CE.

q.s: Who was the founder of the Satavahana dynasty?
q.x: Simuka (Srimukha) founded the Satavahana line after the Mauryas in the Deccan.

q.s: In the Puranas, the Satavahanas are referred to as:
q.x: The Puranas call the Satavahanas Andhra-bhrityas (servants of the Andhras or Andhras who were servants).

q.s: The Allahabad Pillar Prasasti of Samudragupta was composed by:
q.x: Harisena, Samudragupta's Sandhivigrahika, composed the prasasti; Ravikirti wrote the Aihole inscription.

q.s: The Allahabad Prasasti of Samudragupta is written in which script?
q.x: Its 33 lines are in Gupta Brahmi script and classical Sanskrit in champu style.

q.s: The poet Mayura, author of the Suryashataka, adorned the court of:
q.x: Mayura, like Banabhatta, was a court poet of Harshavardhana.

q.s: Bhavabhuti, author of Uttararamacharita, was patronised by:
q.x: Bhavabhuti wrote Malatimadhava and Uttararamacharita under Yashovarman of Kannauj.

q.s: Who was the last ruler of the Eastern Chalukya dynasty of Vengi?
q.x: After Vijayaditya VII died in 1075, Kulottunga I merged Vengi with the Chola state.

q.s: Who merged the Vengi kingdom with the Chola state, uniting the Tamil and Andhra regions?
q.x: Kulottunga I, of Chalukya-Chola descent, merged Vengi with the Chola state after 1075.

q.s: Which was the first southern kingdom attacked by Malik Kafur during his Deccan campaigns?
q.x: Kafur attacked Devagiri in 1307-08, then Warangal (1309-10), Dwarasamudra (1310-11) and Madurai (1311).

q.s: Malik Kafur's invasion of Warangal (1309-10) was directed against which dynasty?
q.x: Warangal was the Kakatiya capital under Prataparudra II; Devagiri belonged to the Yadavas.

q.s: In the First Battle of Panipat (1526), Babur's flanking tactic was known as:
q.x: Tulughma was the flanking attack; araba was the line of carts chained together as a defence.

q.s: Who commanded Babur's artillery at the First Battle of Panipat?
q.x: Ustad Ali Quli, with Mustafa, was in charge of Babur's guns at Panipat.

q.s: Sultan Garhi, regarded as the first Islamic tomb in India, was built by:
q.x: Iltutmish built Sultan Garhi (1231) for his son Nasiruddin Mahmud.

q.s: The Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque in Delhi was built by:
q.x: The Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque in Purana Qila was built by Sher Shah Suri in 1541.

q.s: Amir Khusrau, who called himself 'Tuti-i-Hind', is regarded as the father of which language form?
q.x: Amir Khusrau is called the Father of Khari Boli; his Hindavi verses grew into Rekhta/Urdu.

q.s: Which poet of the Delhi Sultanate was called 'Sadi-i-Hind' for his ghazals?
q.x: Amir Hasan Dehlavi was called the Sadi of India; Khusrau was the Parrot of India.

q.s: Akbar's conquest of Gondwana in 1564 was opposed by which ruler?
q.x: Rani Durgavati of Gondwana resisted Asaf Khan's army in 1564; Baz Bahadur ruled Malwa.

q.s: Kandahar was lost by the Mughals in 1622, during Jahangir's reign, to:
q.x: Shah Abbas I of Persia seized Kandahar in 1622.

q.s: By the Treaty of 1615 with Jahangir, which Mewar ruler submitted to the Mughals?
q.x: Rana Amar Singh submitted in 1615 and his son Karan Singh was made a Mughal mansabdar.

q.s: Which Mughal general seized Emperor Jahangir on the banks of the Jhelum in 1626?
q.x: Mahabat Khan's coup of 1626 took Jahangir captive on the Jhelum.

q.s: The share of Hindu nobles in the Mughal nobility rose to about 31.6 per cent under which emperor?
q.x: Athar Ali's study shows Hindu nobles at about 31.6% in 1679-1707, many being Marathas from the Deccan wars.

q.s: Which Mughal official supervised the royal household and the imperial karkhanas?
q.x: The Mir Saman (Khan-i-Saman) managed the household and karkhanas; the Mir Bakhshi headed the military department.

q.s: In the Mughal administration, religious grants such as madad-i-maash were looked after by the:
q.x: The Sadr-us-Sudur handled religion, charity and madad-i-maash grants; the Qazi-ul-Quzat was the chief justice.

q.s: Who among the following was the only woman saint among the twelve Alvars?
q.x: Andal was the only woman among the Alvars; Karaikkal Ammaiyar was a Nayanar (Shaiva) saint.

q.s: The Periya Puranam, the hagiography of the Nayanars, was written by Sekkizhar under which Chola king?
q.x: Sekkizhar composed the Periya Puranam in the court of Kulottunga II.

q.s: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi, a Mughal-era Sufi of the 16th-17th century, belonged to which order?
q.x: Sirhindi (1564-1624) was a leading Naqshbandi Sufi, who lived long after Kabir.

q.s: The Bhakti saint Kabir was by profession a:
q.x: Kabir was a weaver; Namdev was a tailor, Ravidas a tanner and Dhanna a Jat cultivator.

q.s: Shivaji's son Sambhaji was captured and executed by Aurangzeb in 1689 after being seized at:
q.x: Sambhaji was captured at Sangameshwar and executed in 1689.

q.s: Which Maratha ruler appointed Balaji Vishwanath as Peshwa in 1713?
q.x: Shahu, ruling from Satara, made Balaji Vishwanath Peshwa in 1713.

q.s: The 'Golden Farman' of 1632 granting the English free trade in its ports was issued by the Sultan of:
q.x: The Sultan of Golconda issued the Golden Farman (1632) for an annual payment of 500 pagodas.

q.s: Bombay, received by Charles II as dowry, was given to the East India Company in 1668 for an annual rent of:
q.x: Charles II leased Bombay to the Company in 1668 for 10 pounds a year.

q.s: From whom did the French general Bussy obtain the Northern Circars in 1753?
q.x: Salabat Jang gave the Circars to Bussy to pay for French troops; Muzaffar Jang had died in 1751.

q.s: The city of Hyderabad was founded in 1591 by:
q.x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah founded Hyderabad in 1591 and built the Charminar.

q.s: The Venetian traveller Marco Polo visited which port in Andhra?
q.x: Marco Polo visited Motupalli in the Kakatiya kingdom during Rudramadevi's reign.

q.s: Which Act introduced the system of 'dual control' over the East India Company's Indian affairs?
q.x: Pitt's India Act created the Board of Control alongside the Court of Directors: dual control.

q.s: Which Act made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India?
q.x: The Charter Act of 1833 made Bentinck the first Governor-General of India and ended the Company's trade.

q.s: The end of French power in India came with the British victory in the:
q.x: The Third Carnatic War, decided at Wandiwash (1760), ended French power; the Treaty of Paris (1763) concluded it.

q.s: The First Carnatic War between the English and the French was an extension of the:
q.x: The First Carnatic War (1746-48) was linked to the Austrian War of Succession and ended by the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle.

q.s: The Third Carnatic War was formally concluded by the:
q.x: The Treaty of Paris (1763) ended the Third Carnatic War; the Treaty of Pondicherry closed the Second.

q.s: After the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799), which Wodeyar ruler was restored to the throne of Mysore?
q.x: The boy ruler Krishnaraja Wodeyar III was restored under a subsidiary alliance.

q.s: Which of the following districts was NOT part of the 'Ceded Districts' of 1800?
q.x: The Ceded Districts were Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary, given by the Nizam in 1800.

q.s: The Ceded Districts came to the East India Company in 1800 from:
q.x: The Nizam ceded his share of Mysore territories to pay for the subsidiary force in 1800.

q.s: The Northern Circar of Chicacole corresponds broadly to which present-day district?
q.x: Chicacole is Srikakulam; Mustafanagar (Kondapalli) corresponds to Krishna.

q.s: The College of Fort William at Calcutta was founded in 1800 by which Governor-General?
q.x: Wellesley (1798-1805) founded Fort William College to train Company civil servants.

q.s: The Chanda Railway agitation of 1883 in Hyderabad State was led by:
q.x: Dr Aghorenath Chattopadhyaya, father of Sarojini Naidu, led the agitation against the Chanda Railway scheme.

q.s: The Wadi–Secunderabad railway line of the Nizam's State was opened in:
q.x: The Wadi–Secunderabad line opened in October 1874.

q.s: Who was the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Calcutta set up in 1774?
q.x: Sir Elijah Impey was the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Calcutta under the Regulating Act.

q.s: The Federal Court of India was provided for by the:
q.x: The 1935 Act provided for the Federal Court, set up at Delhi in 1937.

q.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Government of India Act, 1935 is correct?
o: It abolished dyarchy in the provinces.
It made the Governor answerable to the provincial legislature.
It introduced dyarchy in the provinces for the first time.
Its federal dyarchy at the Centre came into operation in 1937.
q.x: The 1935 Act replaced provincial dyarchy with provincial autonomy; the federal part never came into force.

q.s: The Prarthana Samaj at Rajahmundry was founded in 1878 by:
q.x: Veeresalingam founded the Prarthana Samaj at Rajahmundry (1878); Venkataratnam Naidu led the Brahmo movement.

q.s: Dr B.R. Ambedkar was born on 14 April 1891 at:
q.x: Ambedkar was born at Mhow (now Dr Ambedkar Nagar) in Madhya Pradesh, in a Mahar family from Ratnagiri.

q.s: From which institution in London was Dr B.R. Ambedkar called to the bar?
q.x: Ambedkar became a barrister from Gray's Inn; his MSc and DSc were from the London School of Economics.

q.s: The Gurukul Kangri at Haridwar, representing the orthodox wing of the Arya Samaj, was founded by:
q.x: Munshi Ram founded Gurukul Kangri (1902); Lajpat Rai and Hansraj belonged to the DAV (College) party.

q.s: The Namdhari (Kuka) movement in Punjab was founded by:
q.x: Baba Ram Singh founded the Namdhari sect at Bhaini, Ludhiana, in 1857; the Kukas boycotted British goods and courts.

q.s: Who was the first President of the Indian National Congress?
q.x: W.C. Bonnerjee presided over the first session at Bombay in 1885; Hume founded the Indian National Union.

q.s: A.O. Hume, founder of the Indian National Union, is also known as the:
q.x: Hume was a noted ornithologist; the 'Grand Old Man' was Dadabhai Naoroji.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a demand of the early (Moderate) Indian National Congress?
o: Separation of the executive from the judiciary
Simultaneous ICS examinations in India and England
q.x: The Moderates sought reforms within British rule; Purna Swaraj was adopted only at Lahore in 1929.

q.s: 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India', which set out the drain theory, was written by:
q.x: Dadabhai Naoroji wrote the book (1901); R.C. Dutt wrote 'The Economic History of India'.

q.s: The economic nationalist R.C. Dutt presided over which session of the Indian National Congress?
q.x: R.C. Dutt was President of the 1899 Lucknow session.

q.s: The August Declaration of 1917, promising progressive realisation of responsible government, was made by:
q.x: Secretary of State Edwin Montagu made the declaration on 20 August 1917 in the House of Commons.

q.s: Along with Annie Besant, who among the following was interned in June 1917?
q.x: Besant was interned with B.P. Wadia and George Arundale and released in September 1917.

q.s: Jatin Das died in 1929 in Lahore jail after a hunger strike lasting:
q.x: Jatin Das fasted 63 days for political-prisoner status and died on 13 September 1929.

q.s: Mahatma Gandhi attended which Round Table Conference as the sole representative of the Congress?
q.x: Gandhi attended only the Second Conference (1931), after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact; Congress boycotted the other two.

q.s: Gandhi's Phoenix Settlement in South Africa (1904) was located near:
q.x: Phoenix Settlement was near Durban; Tolstoy Farm (1910) was near Johannesburg.

q.s: The Tripuri session of the Congress (1939), where Subhas Chandra Bose was re-elected President, was held near:
q.x: Tripuri is near Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh; Bose had first presided at Haripura (1938).

q.s: Who chaired the National Planning Committee set up by the Congress in 1938?
q.x: Under Bose's presidency, the Congress set up the National Planning Committee with Nehru as chairman.

q.s: B.C. Dutt is remembered for his role in which event of 1946?
o: INA trials at the Red Fort
q.x: B.C. Dutt, a rating of HMIS Talwar, was a central figure in the RIN revolt of February 1946.

q.s: Under the Mountbatten Plan of 3 June 1947, referendums were to be held in the North-West Frontier Province and:
q.x: Referendums were held in the NWFP and Sylhet; Sindh's Assembly decided its own future.

q.s: Who headed the Boundary Commissions set up for the partition of Punjab and Bengal in 1947?
q.x: Sir Cyril Radcliffe chaired both Boundary Commissions.

q.s: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, leader of the Chirala-Perala movement, was popularly known as:
q.x: Duggirala was 'Andhra Ratna'; Prakasam was 'Andhra Kesari' and Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao 'Desoddharaka'.

q.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State formed in 1953?
q.x: Tanguturi Prakasam became the first Chief Minister of Andhra State with Kurnool as capital.

q.s: Potti Sriramulu died on 15 December 1952 after a fast for a separate Andhra State that lasted:
q.x: His 58-day fast led to Nehru's announcement of Andhra State.

q.s: The Razakars, the militant volunteer force of the Majlis-e-Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen in Hyderabad, were led by:
q.x: Qasim Razvi led the Razakars; Mir Laik Ali was the Nizam's last prime minister.

q.s: The 'Tribal Panchsheel', the principles of Nehru's tribal policy, is credited to:
q.x: The Tribal Panchsheel, favouring integration with respect for tribal identity, is credited to Verrier Elwin.

q.s: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, PESA, was enacted in:
q.x: PESA, 1996 extends Part IX to the Fifth Schedule Scheduled Areas.

q.s: Tanguturi Prakasam's ministry in Andhra State fell in November 1954 over which issue?
q.x: Prakasam's ministry was defeated on 15 November 1954 over prohibition, leading to President's rule.

q.s: The 'Ramadandu' volunteer corps was organised in the Chirala-Perala movement of 1921 by:
q.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya organised the Ramadandu during the Chirala-Perala movement.

q.s: Tanguturi Prakasam served early in his career as municipal chairman of which town?
q.x: Prakasam was municipal chairman of Rajahmundry.

q.s: Who was the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh during the Jai Andhra movement of 1972?
q.x: P.V. Narasimha Rao was CM; President's Rule followed on 18 January 1973.

q.s: Daimabad, which yielded a bronze chariot and buffalo, is located on the banks of which river?
q.x: Daimabad, the largest Jorwe site and the southernmost Late Harappan site, lies on the Pravara in Ahmednagar.

q.s: A minor rock edict of Ashoka has been found in Andhra Pradesh at:
q.x: Rajula Mandagiri (Kurnool) has a minor rock edict; Amaravati yielded a pillar-edict fragment.

q.s: The Indian National Calendar based on the Saka era was adopted on 22 March 1957. Its first month is:
q.x: The national calendar begins with Chaitra; 1 Chaitra falls on 22 March (21 March in a leap year).

q.s: The Saka era, used in the Indian National Calendar, began in:
q.x: The Saka era begins in 78 CE; 57 BCE is the Vikrama era and 320 CE the Gupta era.

q.s: The Satavahana king Hala, known as 'Kavivatsala', compiled which Prakrit work?
q.x: Hala compiled the Gathasaptasati; Gunadhya wrote the Brihatkatha.

q.s: Who first identified the Amaravati stupa site in 1797?
q.x: Colin Mackenzie identified Amaravati in 1797; Sewell excavated it in 1877.

q.s: On the ayakapatas of Amaravati, the Buddha's birth is depicted by the symbol of the:
q.x: Lotus = birth, horse = renunciation, Bodhi tree = enlightenment, wheel = first sermon, stupa = parinirvana.

q.s: Nagarjunakonda was the main centre of which school of art in its final, mature phase?
q.x: Ikshvaku carving at Nagarjunakonda is the last phase of the Amaravati school, with Buddha's life and Jatakas as themes.

q.s: The Eastern Chalukya dynasty of Vengi was founded by:
q.x: Pulakeshin II conquered Vengi and made his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana its ruler.

q.s: The Addanki inscription of Pandaranga, the first Telugu verse inscription, is composed in which metre?
q.x: Pandaranga, general of Gunaga Vijayaditya III, left the Addanki inscription in Taruvoja metre.

q.s: Kubja Vishnuvardhana was made viceroy of Vengi by Pulakeshin II in about:
q.x: Pulakeshin II took Vengi from the Vishnukundins c. 616 and installed Kubja Vishnuvardhana in 617.

q.s: The phrase 'Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa' occurs in which work?
q.x: Krishnadevaraya wrote it in the Amuktamalyada.

q.s: Telugu Language Day (29 August) marks the birth anniversary of:
q.x: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy, champion of spoken (vyavaharika) Telugu, was born on 29 August 1863.

q.s: 'Kavibrahma', one of the Kavitraya of the Telugu Mahabharata, is the title of:
q.x: Tikkana is Kavibrahma; Nannaya is Adikavi and Errana is Prabandha Parameswara.

q.s: Palkuriki Somanatha, a leader of the Desi kavita movement, wrote which of the following works?
q.x: Somanatha wrote Basava Puranam, Panditaradhya Charitra and Vrushadhipa Satakam.

q.s: The Thousand Pillar temple at Hanumakonda was built by the Kakatiya ruler:
q.x: Rudradeva (Prataparudra I) built the Thousand Pillar temple in 1163.

q.s: After the Tughlaq conquest of 1323, the Kakatiya capital Orugallu (Warangal) was renamed:
q.x: The Tughlaqs renamed Warangal Sultanpur after 1323.

q.s: The Anumakonda (Thousand Pillar) inscription of 1163, recording Kakatiya independence, was composed by:
q.x: Achitendru composed the inscription of Rudradeva; Jayapa wrote the Nritta Ratnavali.

q.s: Mahmud Gawan, the famous minister of the Bahmani kingdom, was executed in 1481 by:
q.x: Muhammad Shah III executed Gawan in 1481 on a forged letter; the kingdom broke up soon after.

q.s: Saluva Narasimha shifted his capital from Kalyanapuram to:
q.x: Saluva Narasimha ruled from Chandragiri; Penukonda became the Aravidu capital after Talikota.

q.s: 'Saluvabhyudayam', a work on Saluva Narasimha, was written by his court poet:
q.x: Rajanatha Dindima wrote Saluvabhyudayam; Gangadevi wrote Madhuravijayam.

q.s: Which poet of Krishnadevaraya's court bore the title 'Andhra Kavita Pitamaha'?
q.x: Allasani Peddana, author of Manucharitra, was Andhra Kavita Pitamaha.

q.s: After his Kalinga campaign, Krishnadevaraya married the daughter of which Gajapati ruler?
q.x: Krishnadevaraya married Prataparudra Gajapati's daughter (Tukka/Bhadradevi) and returned lands north of the Krishna.

q.s: After suppressing the Palegars of the Ceded Districts, Thomas Munro introduced which land revenue system there?
q.x: Munro introduced the Ryotwari system in the Ceded Districts, settling revenue directly with the cultivator.

q.s: The Malkapuram inscription of 1261, describing a college and hospital at Mandadam, belongs to the reign of:
q.x: The Malkapuram inscription is of Rudramadevi's reign; it records Visvesvara Sambhu's institutions.

q.s: The Veerabhadra temple at Lepakshi was built by Virupanna and Veeranna, officers of which Vijayanagara ruler?
q.x: The Penukonda governors Virupanna and Veeranna built Lepakshi c. 1530-40 under Achyutadevaraya.

q.s: In the Qutb Shahi period, elephants were imported into Andhra ports mainly from:
q.x: Elephants came from Ceylon; Persia and Arabia supplied horses.

q.s: In Qutb Shahi Golconda, textiles ranked second in importance only to:
q.x: The diamond mines of Golconda were the leading wealth; textiles came second.

q.s: 'Yayati Charitra' (1572), a kavya in pure (achcha) Telugu, was written by:
q.x: Ponnekanti Telaganaryudu's Yayati Charitra avoided Sanskrit words entirely.

q.s: Bipin Chandra Pal's tour of Andhra in 1907 was organised by Mutnuri Krishna Rao, editor of:
q.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao edited the Krishna Patrika; Andhra Patrika was Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's.

q.s: Bipin Chandra Pal's lectures in Rajahmundry in 1907 are associated with which movement?
q.x: Pal's 1907 tour spread the Vandemataram movement in Andhra after the partition of Bengal.

q.s: The Andhra Jateeya Kalasala at Machilipatnam was founded in 1910 by:
q.x: Kopalle Hanumantha Rao was its founder and first principal and made weaving a subject there.

q.s: Which Andhra leader was given the title 'Desoddharaka'?
q.x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was Desoddharaka; Konda Venkatappayya was Desabhakta.

q.s: The title 'Desabhakta' was associated with:
q.x: Konda Venkatappayya was Desabhakta; Nyapati Subba Rao was called Andhra Bhishma.

q.s: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Bill was introduced in 1947 by Revenue Minister:
q.x: Kala Venkata Rao introduced the Bill on 11 November 1947; the Act got assent in April 1949.

q.s: The 1937 committee that held that the land belongs to the tiller and the zamindar is only a tax collector was headed by:
q.x: The Prakasam Committee of the Madras Legislature reported in November 1938.

q.s: Who was the first Governor of Andhra State formed in 1953?
q.x: C.M. Trivedi, earlier Special Officer for Andhra State, became its first Governor.

q.s: In 2014, the committee for allocation of State government employees between AP and Telangana was headed by:
q.x: The Kamalanathan committee allocated employees; Sheela Bhide dealt with Schedule IX institutions.

q.s: The classic Telugu film 'Pathala Bhairavi' (1951) was directed by:
q.x: Pathala Bhairavi was K.V. Reddy's; K. Viswanath is best known for Sankarabharanam.

q.s: When Pingali Venkayya showed his flag design at the Bezwada AICC session of 1921, Gandhi suggested adding:
q.x: Gandhi asked for the charkha; the Ashoka Chakra replaced it only in 1947.

q.s: Pingali Venkayya, designer of the early tricolour and called 'Jhanda Venkayya', was born at:
q.x: Venkayya was born in 1876 at Bhatlapenumarru in Krishna district.

q.s: Udayana, the king of Vatsa who married Vasavadatta, had his capital at:
